tower-of-hanoi.title: Goal Stack Ordering
tower-of-hanoi.principle: The final configuration on the goal peg must be a descending stack (largest at the bottom, smallest at the top). To achieve this, always place larger disks onto the goal peg before any smaller disks that belong above them.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: When planning the sequence of moves toward the goal configuration, verify the desired order on the goal peg and schedule moves so that each larger disk is placed before the smaller disks that should sit on top of it.
tower-of-hanoi.example: If the goal peg already contains disk 5, you may place disk 4 next, but you must not place disk 1 before disk 4.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Free Blocked Disk
tower-of-hanoi.principle: A disk that has any smaller disks on top cannot be moved directly; you must first relocate those smaller disks to another peg.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: Whenever you need to move a disk that is not the topmost on its peg.
tower-of-hanoi.example: To move disk 4 from peg 0, first move disks 1 and 2 elsewhere.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Use Auxiliary Peg for Temporary Storage
tower-of-hanoi.principle: In a three‑peg problem, the peg that is neither the source nor the destination of a move serves as a temporary storage location for displaced disks.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: Whenever you need to free a disk or move a smaller stack while preserving the larger disk's position.
tower-of-hanoi.example: When moving disk 4 from peg 0 to peg 2, use peg 1 as the auxiliary to hold disks 1 and 2.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Recursive Sub‑tower Transfer
tower-of-hanoi.principle: Moving a stack of k disks from one peg to another follows the recursion: first move the top k‑1 disks to the auxiliary peg, then move the kth (largest) disk, then move the k‑1 disks onto it.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: Whenever you need to relocate a contiguous block of disks while preserving order.
tower-of-hanoi.example: To move disks 1‑3 from peg 0 to peg 2, first move disks 1‑2 to peg 1, then move disk 3, then move disks 1‑2 onto disk 3.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Check Move Legality
tower-of-hanoi.principle: A legal move must take the topmost disk from the source peg and place it onto a destination peg that is empty or whose top disk is larger.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: Before committing any move, verify that the source peg’s top disk is being moved and that the destination peg’s top (if any) is larger.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Moving disk 4 onto a peg whose top is disk 2 is illegal because 4 > 2.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Simulate Final Configuration
tower-of-hanoi.principle: After writing a complete move list, mentally replay each move from the initial state to ensure that the final configuration matches the goal.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: After you think you have a solution, run through the moves step‑by‑step before submitting.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Check that after the last move the goal peg contains [5,4,3,2,1] in that order.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Maintain 0‑Indexed Peg Numbers
tower-of-hanoi.principle: The output format expects peg identifiers 0, 1, 2; using any other numbering (e.g., 1‑based) will be rejected.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: When writing the move list, always label pegs with 0, 1, 2.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Write [1,0,2] for moving disk 1 from peg 0 to peg 2, not [1,1,3].

tower-of-hanoi.title: Track Current Top Disk on Each Peg
tower-of-hanoi.principle: Keep an up‑to‑date mental (or written) record of the topmost disk on every peg after each move, so you know which moves are legal.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: During planning and execution of the move sequence.
tower-of-hanoi.example: After moving disk 1 from peg 0 to peg 2, the new top of peg 0 is disk 2.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Leverage Existing Larger Disks on Target as Base
tower-of-hanoi.principle: If the goal peg already contains larger disks that are correctly placed, you can place a smaller disk onto it, using those larger disks as a stable base.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: When the destination peg already has some of the final stack in place.
tower-of-hanoi.example: After moving disk 5 to peg 2, you can place disk 4 onto peg 2 because 5 > 4.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Clear Destination Peg of Smaller Top Disk Before Placing Larger Disk
tower-of-hanoi.principle: If the destination peg’s top disk is smaller than the disk you intend to move, you must first relocate that smaller (and any disks above it) to another peg, making the destination top larger or empty before placing the larger disk.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: Whenever a move would place a larger disk onto a peg that currently has a smaller top disk.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Before moving disk 5 onto peg 2, move disk 3 (the smaller top) to another peg.

tower-of-hanoi.description: Placing a larger disk onto a smaller one
tower-of-hanoi.why_it_happens: The model forgets the rule that larger disks cannot be placed on top of smaller ones.
tower-of-hanoi.how_to_avoid: Always compare the size of the moving disk with the top disk of the destination; only move if the destination is empty or its top is larger.

tower-of-hanoi.why_it_happens: The model may overlook that only the topmost disk of a peg can be moved.
tower-of-hanoi.how_to_avoid: Track the current top disk on each peg and only select that disk for a move.

tower-of-hanoi.description: Prematurely placing a small disk on the goal peg
tower-of-hanoi.why_it_happens: The model tries to fill the goal peg early, forgetting that larger disks must be placed first.
tower-of-hanoi.how_to_avoid: Follow the placement order: place larger disks before any smaller ones that belong above them.

tower-of-hanoi.why_it_happens: The model mixes 0‑based and 1‑based peg numbering.
tower-of-hanoi.how_to_avoid: Always use 0, 1, 2 as peg identifiers in the output.

tower-of-hanoi.description: Skipping final verification of the goal state
tower-of-hanoi.why_it_happens: The model assumes the move list is correct without checking.
tower-of-hanoi.how_to_avoid: Replay the entire move sequence mentally (or on paper) and confirm the final configuration matches the goal.
